steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Food preservation extends shelf life by preventing or slowing microbial growth (bacteria, moulds, yeasts) and enzymatic spoilage. Microorganisms need warmth, moisture, food, oxygen, and appropriate pH to grow. | Key Fact: Pasteurisation: heating food to 72°C for 15 seconds (HTST) or 63°C for 30 minutes (LTLT), then rapid cooling. Kills pathogenic bacteria but not all spoilage organisms. Used for: milk, fruit juices, eggs. Refrigerated pasteurised products have limited shelf life. | Key Fact: UHT (Ultra-High Temperature): heating to 135°C for 1-2 seconds. Kills all microorganisms including spores.
